provenance.constructionPolicy: Source-aligned editorial adaptation of Hephaestus Returns to Olympus based only on the linked source-audited record; not a source edition.

scope.beginning: The episode begins with Zeus casting Hephaestus from heaven and Hephaestus refusing to return to Olympus.
scope.ending: It ends when Dionysus uses wine to lure Hephaestus back and Hephaestus is led to Olympus.
scope.boundaryRationale: The linked source ends after Hephaestus reaches Olympus; Hera's release and any later settlement are excluded because the surviving source sentence is truncated.

variant.chosenVersion: Baker's Vulcan-and-Bacchus version: the golden throne traps Hera, Hermes fails, and Dionysus lures Hephaestus back with wine.
materialAlternatives: Later versions in which Hera is explicitly released or Hephaestus receives a formal restoration are excluded.

characters.name: Hephaestus
characters.goal: remain apart from Olympus until Dionysus brings him back

characters.name: Hera
characters.role: mother trapped by the golden throne

characters.name: Zeus
characters.role: father who banishes Hephaestus and seeks his return

relationships.rationale: The linked source identifies Hera as Hephaestus' mother.
The linked source identifies Zeus as Hephaestus' father.
Dionysus lures Hephaestus with wine and leads him to Olympus.

narrative.synopsis: After Zeus casts Hephaestus from heaven, the smith god refuses Olympus and later sends Hera a golden throne whose hidden springs trap her. Hermes cannot persuade him to return, but Dionysus makes him drink and leads him back to Olympus.
narrative.openingSituation: Hephaestus has been cast from heaven and refuses to return to the gods who treated him badly.
narrative.centralConflict: Hera is trapped in Hephaestus' golden throne, but Hephaestus rejects Hermes' invitation to Olympus.
narrative.resolution: Dionysus wins Hephaestus' welcome with wine and continues pouring until Hephaestus can be led away.
narrative.outcome: Hephaestus is led back to Olympus; the linked source does not complete Hera's release.

events.consequence: Hephaestus falls from heaven and withdraws from Olympus.
Hephaestus remains at his forge in Mount Etna.
A golden throne arrives for Hera as a gift.
Hidden springs contract and hold Hera prisoner.
Hermes' polite appeal fails to move Hephaestus.
Dionysus gives him wine and leads him to Olympus.

visualBeats: Zeus casts Hephaestus from heaven and the smith withdraws to Mount Etna.
Hera sits in the golden throne and its hidden mechanism closes around her.
Dionysus pours wine until Hephaestus can be led back toward Olympus.
productionNotes: End at Hephaestus' arrival in Olympus; do not show Hera's release or a restored divine status as completed facts.
